summary: playwright-stealth is a thin Python wrapper that ports puppeteer-extra-plugin-stealth's JavaScript evasion scripts to Playwright Python. It injects 17+ stealth scripts via Playwright's `add_init_script()` API to mask automation fingerprints — hiding `navigator.webdriver`, faking `navigator.plugins`/`mimeTypes`, spoofing WebGL vendor/renderer, mocking `chrome.runtime`/`chrome.loadtimes`/`chrome.csi`/`chrome.app`, patching `navigator.permissions`, `navigator.languages`, `navigator.platform`, `navigator.hardwareConcurrency`, media codecs, iframe contentWindow, window.outerdimensions, and hairline detection. The Python layer (stealth.py, ~150 lines) is merely a config dataclass and script loader; all real evasion logic lives in the JS files under `playwright_stealth/js/`. The library uses Proxy-based interception with error-stack sanitization to avoid detection of the Proxy wrappers themselves. It's essentially a direct port of the puppeteer-extra stealth plugin with minimal Playwright-specific adaptation.

findings.description:
- navigator.webdriver hiding (delete from prototype or return undefined)
- navigator.plugins & mimeTypes simulation with Chrome-typical entries (PDF viewer, Native Client)
- navigator.vendor, platform, languages, hardwareConcurrency spoofing
- navigator.permissions mock (returns 'granted' for notifications)
- navigator.userAgent override capability
- WebGL vendor/renderer spoofing (Intel Iris OpenGL Engine default)
- chrome.runtime mock with sendMessage/connect and realistic error signatures
- chrome.loadtimes, chrome.csi, chrome.app mocks
- iframe.contentWindow property patching
- window.outerWidth/outerHeight/devicePixelRatio spoofing
- Hairline detection evasion (canvas fingerprinting)
- Media codecs simulation (H.264, VP8, VP9, etc.)
- Proxy error-stack sanitization to hide instrumentation
- toString() proxy patching to show native code strings
- Configurable per-script enable/disable via StealthConfig dataclass
- Sync (stealth_sync) and async (stealth_async) APIs

apiSurface:
- `stealth_async(page: AsyncPage, config: StealthConfig = None) -> None` — main async entry point
- `stealth_sync(page: SyncPage, config: StealthConfig = None) -> None` — sync entry point
- `StealthConfig` dataclass with 20+ boolean/option fields controlling each evasion
- Usage: `await stealth_async(page)` or `await stealth_async(page, StealthConfig(webgl_vendor=False, ...))`
- All evasions enabled by default; disable via `StealthConfig(webdrive=False, ...)`
- Custom scripts injectable by subclassing StealthConfig and overriding `enabled_scripts` property
integrationPoints:
- **Playwright pipeline**: Call `await stealth_async(page)` immediately after `browser.new_page()` and before any `page.goto()`
- **Queue integration**: Stateless — no persistent state; safe to reuse config across pages/workers
- **Search/matching**: No built-in detection testing; would need external verification (bot.sannysoft.com, pixelscan.net, etc.)
- **Deterministic ETL**: Works well — same config yields same fingerprint; no randomness unless user adds it
- **Headless/headful**: Scripts auto-detect headful mode and skip (won't break real Chrome)
- **Multi-browser**: Scripts target Chromium; Firefox/WebKit support untested (some evasions Chrome-specific like chrome.runtime)
- **Resource loading**: Uses importlib.resources — works in packaged/installed distributions
strengthsForVeridian:
- **Minimal, auditable surface** — ~150 lines Python + readable JS; easy to verify/extend
- **Direct puppeteer-extra port** — inherits battle-tested evasions from actively maintained JS ecosystem
- **Playwright-native** — uses `add_init_script()` correctly; no CDP hacks or brittle workarounds
- **Configurable per-evasion** — disable specific scripts that break target sites
- **Sync + async** — supports both Playwright APIs
- **No external deps** — only Playwright; no selenium, no browser binary management
- **Extensible generator pattern** — easy to inject custom scripts for site-specific needs
- **Deterministic** — same config = same fingerprint; good for reproducible scraping
weaknessesForVeridian:
- **Chromium-centric** — many evasions (chrome.*, webgl vendor) are Chrome-specific; Firefox/WebKit may leak
- **Single maintainer, low activity** — 13 commits, v0.3.0, no recent releases visible; bus factor = 1
- **No auto-update of fingerprints** — static Chrome versions in JS; real Chrome updates may change detection vectors
- **No built-in verification** — must test against external bot detection sites manually
- **Missing modern evasions** — no Canvas/WebGL noise, no AudioContext fingerprinting, no Battery API, no WebRTC IP leak protection
- **Hardcoded defaults** — Intel GPU, Google Inc vendor, en-US languages; may not match target locale/hardware
- **No stealth for `navigator.webdriver` in Firefox** — script only handles Chrome's webdriver property
- **utils.js uses `eval()`** — for function materialization; may trip CSP in locked-down environments
- **No TypeScript types** — Python-only; JS scripts lack type definitions for IDE support
limitations: Seeded from prior analysis; maturity signals may be approximate
